verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.93
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 10.93

verses.pali: 10. Upālivagga
verses.english: 10. With Upāli

verses.pali: Kiṁdiṭṭhikasutta
verses.english: What Is Your View?

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

verses.pali: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati divā divassa sāvatthiyā nikkhami bhagavantaṁ dassanāya.
verses.english: Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika left Sāvatthī in the middle of the day to see the Buddha.

verses.pali: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa etadahosi:
verses.english: Then it occurred to him,

verses.pali: “akālo kho tāva bhagavantaṁ dassanāya.
verses.english: “It’s the wrong time to see the Buddha,

verses.pali: Paṭisallīno bhagavā.
verses.english: as he’s in retreat.

verses.pali: Manobhāvanīyānampi bhikkhūnaṁ akālo dassanāya.
verses.english: And it’s the wrong time to see the esteemed mendicants,

verses.pali: Paṭisallīnā manobhāvanīyā bhikkhū.
verses.english: as they’re in retreat.

verses.pali: Yannūnāhaṁ yena aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ ārāmo tenupasaṅkameyyan”ti.
verses.english: Why don’t I visit the monastery of the wanderers of other religions?”

verses.pali: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ ārāmo tenupasaṅkami.
verses.english: Then he went to the monastery of the wanderers of other religions.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena aññatitthiyā paribbājakā saṅgamma samāgamma unnādino uccāsaddamahāsaddā anekavihitaṁ tiracchānakathaṁ kathentā nisinnā honti.
verses.english: Now at that time, the wanderers of other religions had come together, making an uproar, a colossal racket as they sat and talked about all kinds of low topics.

verses.pali: Addasaṁsu kho te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
verses.english: They saw Anāthapiṇḍika coming off in the distance,

verses.pali: Disvāna aññamaññaṁ saṇṭhāpesuṁ:
verses.english: and stopped each other, saying,

verses.pali: “appasaddā bhonto hontu, mā bhonto saddamakattha.
verses.english: “Be quiet, good fellows, don’t make a sound.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati ārāmaṁ āgacchati samaṇassa gotamassa sāvako.
verses.english: The householder Anāthapiṇḍika, a disciple of the ascetic Gotama, is coming into our monastery.

verses.pali: Yāvatā kho pana samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakā gihī odātavasanā sāvatthiyaṁ paṭivasanti, ayaṁ tesaṁ aññataro anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati.
verses.english: He is included among the white-clothed lay disciples of the ascetic Gotama, who is residing in Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: Appasaddakāmā kho pana te āyasmanto appasaddavinītā appasaddassa vaṇṇavādino.
verses.english: Such venerables like the quiet, are educated to be quiet, and praise the quiet.

verses.pali: Appeva nāma appasaddaṁ parisaṁ viditvā upasaṅkamitabbaṁ maññeyyā”ti.
verses.english: Hopefully if he sees that our assembly is quiet he’ll see fit to approach.”

verses.pali: Atha kho te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā tuṇhī ahesuṁ.
verses.english: Then those wanderers of other religions fell silent.

verses.pali: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā tehi aññatitthiyehi paribbājakehi saddhiṁ sammodi.
verses.english: Then Anāthapiṇḍika went up to them, and exchanged greetings with those wanderers.

verses.pali: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side. The wanderers said to him,

verses.pali: “vadehi, gahapati, kiṁdiṭṭhiko samaṇo gotamo”ti?
verses.english: “Tell us, householder, what is the view of the ascetic Gotama?”

verses.pali: “Na kho ahaṁ, bhante, bhagavato sabbaṁ diṭṭhiṁ jānāmī”ti.
verses.english: “Sirs, I don’t know all his views.”

verses.pali: “Iti kira tvaṁ, gahapati, na samaṇassa gotamassa sabbaṁ diṭṭhiṁ jānāsi;
verses.english: “Well then, since it seems you don’t know all the views of the ascetic Gotama,

verses.pali: vadehi, gahapati, kiṁdiṭṭhikā bhikkhū”ti?
verses.english: tell us, what are the views of the mendicants?”

verses.pali: “Bhikkhūnampi kho ahaṁ, bhante, na sabbaṁ diṭṭhiṁ jānāmī”ti.
verses.english: “Sirs, I don’t know all the mendicants’ views.”

verses.pali: “Iti kira tvaṁ, gahapati, na samaṇassa gotamassa sabbaṁ diṭṭhiṁ jānāsi napi bhikkhūnaṁ sabbaṁ diṭṭhiṁ jānāsi;
verses.english: “Well then, since it seems you don’t know all the views of the ascetic Gotama or of the mendicants,

verses.pali: vadehi, gahapati, kiṁdiṭṭhikosi tuvan”ti?
verses.english: tell us, householder, what is your view?”

verses.pali: “Etaṁ kho, bhante, amhehi na dukkaraṁ byākātuṁ yaṁdiṭṭhikā mayaṁ.
verses.english: “Sirs, it’s not hard for me to explain what my views are.

verses.pali: Iṅgha tāva āyasmanto yathāsakāni diṭṭhigatāni byākarontu, pacchāpetaṁ amhehi na dukkaraṁ bhavissati byākātuṁ yaṁdiṭṭhikā mayan”ti.
verses.english: But please, let the venerables explain their own convictions first. Afterwards it won’t be hard for me to explain my views.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro paribbājako anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he said this, one of the wanderers said to him,

verses.pali: “sassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
verses.english: “The cosmos is eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.

verses.pali: evaṁdiṭṭhiko ahaṁ, gahapatī”ti.
verses.english: That’s my view, householder.”

verses.pali: Aññataropi kho paribbājako anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Another wanderer said,

verses.pali: “asassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
verses.english: “The cosmos is not eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.

verses.pali: evaṁdiṭṭhiko ahaṁ, gahapatī”ti.
verses.english: That’s my view, householder.”

verses.pali: Aññataropi kho paribbājako anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Another wanderer said,

verses.pali: “antavā loko …pe…
verses.english: “The cosmos is finite …” …

verses.pali: anantavā loko …
verses.english: “The cosmos is infinite …” …

verses.pali: taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīraṁ …
verses.english: “The soul and the body are one and the same …” …

verses.pali: aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīraṁ …
verses.english: “The soul is one thing, the body another …” …

verses.pali: hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā …
verses.english: “A realized one still exists after death …” …

verses.pali: na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā …
verses.english: “A realized one no longer exists after death …” …

verses.pali: hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā …
verses.english: “A realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death …” …

verses.pali: neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
verses.english: “A Realized One neither exists nor doesn’t exist after death. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.

verses.pali: evaṁdiṭṭhiko ahaṁ, gahapatī”ti.
verses.english: That’s my view, householder.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati te paribbājake etadavoca:
verses.english: When this was said, Anāthapiṇḍika said this,

verses.pali: “yvāyaṁ, bhante, āyasmā evamāha:
verses.english: “Sirs, regarding the venerable who said this:

verses.pali: ‘sassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
verses.english: ‘The cosmos is eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.

verses.pali: evaṁdiṭṭhiko ahaṁ, gahapatī’ti,
verses.english: That’s my view, householder.’

verses.pali: imassa ayamāyasmato diṭṭhi attano vā ayonisomanasikārahetu uppannā paratoghosapaccayā vā.
verses.english: This view of his has either arisen from his own irrational application of mind, or is conditioned by what someone else says.

verses.pali: Sā kho panesā diṭṭhi bhūtā saṅkhatā cetayitā paṭiccasamuppannā.
verses.english: But that view is created, conditioned, chosen, dependently originated.

verses.pali: Yaṁ kho pana kiñci bhūtaṁ saṅkhataṁ cetayitaṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ tadaniccaṁ.
verses.english: Whatever is created, conditioned, chosen, and dependently originated is impermanent.

verses.pali: Yadaniccaṁ taṁ dukkhaṁ.
verses.english: And what’s impermanent is suffering.

verses.pali: Yaṁ dukkhaṁ tadeveso āyasmā allīno, tadeveso āyasmā ajjhupagato.
verses.english: What he clings to and holds to is just suffering.

verses.pali: Yopāyaṁ, bhante, āyasmā evamāha:
verses.english: Regarding the venerable who said this:

verses.pali: ‘asassato loko, idameva saccaṁ moghamaññanti—
verses.english: ‘The cosmos is not eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.

verses.pali: evaṁdiṭṭhiko ahaṁ, gahapatī’ti,
verses.english: That’s my view, householder.’

verses.pali: imassāpi ayamāyasmato diṭṭhi attano vā ayonisomanasikārahetu uppannā paratoghosapaccayā vā.
verses.english: This view of his has either arisen from his own irrational application of mind, or is conditioned by what someone else says.

verses.pali: Sā kho panesā diṭṭhi bhūtā saṅkhatā cetayitā paṭiccasamuppannā.
verses.english: But that view is created, conditioned, chosen, dependently originated.

verses.pali: Yaṁ kho pana kiñci bhūtaṁ saṅkhataṁ cetayitaṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ tadaniccaṁ.
verses.english: Whatever is created, conditioned, chosen, and dependently originated is impermanent.

verses.pali: Yadaniccaṁ taṁ dukkhaṁ.
verses.english: And what’s impermanent is suffering.

verses.pali: Yaṁ dukkhaṁ tadeveso āyasmā allīno, tadeveso āyasmā ajjhupagato.
verses.english: What he clings to and holds to is just suffering.

verses.pali: Yopāyaṁ, bhante, āyasmā evamāha:
verses.english: Regarding the venerable who said this:

verses.pali: ‘antavā loko …pe…
verses.english: ‘The cosmos is finite …’ …

verses.pali: anantavā loko …
verses.english: ‘The cosmos is infinite …’ …

verses.pali: taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīraṁ …
verses.english: ‘The soul and the body are one and the same …’ …

verses.pali: aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīraṁ …
verses.english: ‘The soul is one thing, the body another …’ …

verses.pali: hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā …
verses.english: ‘A realized one still exists after death …’ …

verses.pali: na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā …
verses.english: ‘A realized one no longer exists after death …’ …

verses.pali: hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā …
verses.english: ‘A realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death …’ …

verses.english: But that view is created, conditioned, chosen, dependently originated.

verses.english: Whatever is created, conditioned, chosen, and dependently originated is impermanent.

verses.pali: Yaṁ dukkhaṁ tadeveso āyasmā allīno, tadeveso āyasmā ajjhupagato”ti.
verses.english: What he clings to and holds to is just suffering.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte te paribbājakā anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: When he said this the wanderers said to him,

verses.pali: “byākatāni kho, gahapati, amhehi sabbeheva yathāsakāni diṭṭhigatāni.
verses.english: “Householder, we’ve each explained our own convictions.

verses.pali: Vadehi, gahapati, kiṁdiṭṭhikosi tuvan”ti?
verses.english: Tell us, householder, what is your view?”

verses.pali: “Yaṁ kho, bhante, kiñci bhūtaṁ saṅkhataṁ cetayitaṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ tadaniccaṁ.
verses.english: “Sirs, whatever is created, conditioned, chosen, and dependently originated is impermanent.

verses.pali: Yadaniccaṁ taṁ dukkhaṁ.
verses.english: And what’s impermanent is suffering.

verses.pali: ‘Yaṁ dukkhaṁ taṁ netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti—
verses.english: And what’s suffering is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.

verses.pali: evaṁdiṭṭhiko ahaṁ, bhante”ti.
verses.english: That’s my view, sirs.”

verses.pali: “Yaṁ kho, gahapati, kiñci bhūtaṁ saṅkhataṁ cetayitaṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ tadaniccaṁ.
verses.english: “Householder, whatever is created, conditioned, chosen, and dependently originated is impermanent.

verses.pali: Yadaniccaṁ taṁ dukkhaṁ.
verses.english: And what’s impermanent is suffering.

verses.pali: Yaṁ dukkhaṁ tadeva tvaṁ, gahapati, allīno, tadeva tvaṁ, gahapati, ajjhupagato”ti.
verses.english: What you cling to and hold to is just suffering.”

verses.pali: “Yaṁ kho, bhante, kiñci bhūtaṁ saṅkhataṁ cetayitaṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ tadaniccaṁ.
verses.english: “Sirs, whatever is created, conditioned, chosen, and dependently originated is impermanent.

verses.pali: Yadaniccaṁ taṁ dukkhaṁ.
verses.english: And what’s impermanent is suffering.

verses.pali: ‘Yaṁ dukkhaṁ taṁ netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, nameso attā’ti—evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhaṁ.
verses.english: And I’ve truly seen clearly with right wisdom that what’s suffering is not mine, I am not this, it’s not my self.

verses.pali: Tassa ca uttari nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ pajānāmī”ti.
verses.english: And I truly understand the escape beyond that.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte te paribbājakā tuṇhībhūtā maṅkubhūtā pattakkhandhā adhomukhā pajjhāyantā appaṭibhānā nisīdiṁsu.
verses.english: When this was said, those wanderers sat silent, dismayed, shoulders drooping, downcast, depressed, with nothing to say.

verses.pali: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati te paribbājake tuṇhībhūte maṅkubhūte pattakkhandhe adhomukhe pajjhāyante appaṭibhāne viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yāvatako ahosi tehi aññatitthiyehi paribbājakehi saddhiṁ kathāsallāpo taṁ sabbaṁ bhagavato ārocesi.
verses.english: Seeing this, Anāthapiṇḍika got up from his seat. He went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and informed the Buddha of all they had discussed.

verses.pali: “Sādhu sādhu, gahapati.
verses.english: “Good, good, householder!

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho te, gahapati, moghapurisā kālena kālaṁ sahadhammena suniggahitaṁ niggahetabbā”ti.
verses.english: That’s how you should legitimately and completely refute those futile men from time to time.”

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṁsesi.
verses.english: Then the Buddha educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired the householder Anāthapiṇḍika with a Dhamma talk,

verses.pali: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṁsito uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
verses.english: after which Anāthapiṇḍika got up from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha before leaving.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkante anāthapiṇḍike gahapatimhi bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: Then, not long after Anāthapiṇḍika had left, the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

verses.pali: “yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vassasatupasampanno imasmiṁ dhammavinaye, sopi evamevaṁ aññatitthiye paribbājake sahadhammena suniggahitaṁ niggaṇheyya yathā taṁ anāthapiṇḍikena gahapatinā niggahitā”ti.
verses.english: “Mendicants, even a mendicant who has ordained for a hundred years in this teaching and training would legitimately and completely refute those wanderers of other religions just as the householder Anāthapiṇḍika did.”

verses.pali: Tatiyaṁ.
